summary: oh-my-zelenka exfiltrates host and process data to httpbin.org on import
details: On `import oh_my_zelenka`, the top-level __init__.py unconditionally starts a daemon background thread that collects installer-side host and process information — platform details, uid/pid, cwd, the contents of /proc/version, `ps aux` output, `pm list packages` output, and EXTERA_* environment variables — and POSTs it as a JSON body to https://httpbin.org/post. On Android hosts it additionally writes the collected data to /storage/emulated/0/Download/extera_poc and reads EXTERA_FILES_DIR / EXTERA_CACHE_DIR. The payload embeds a self-identifying marker (`event: supply_chain_executed`, `source: oh-my-zelenka PyPI package`) framing itself as a supply-chain proof-of-concept targeting the exteraGram Android messenger, but the code path runs unconditionally at import and performs real host reconnaissance and outbound exfiltration regardless of that framing. The destination (httpbin.org) is a public request-echo service rather than attacker-owned infrastructure, but installer process and environment data still leaves the host to a third party the installer did not configure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
